interactions.summary: A student asks whether Piccarda failed to want escape or failed to want ascent, and Jiang answers by staging the convent raid as a test of fear, prayer, and trust in God, concluding that fear itself reveals the weakness that keeps her in the lower sphere.
A student asks whether change is still possible in heaven, and Jiang answers yes, insisting that the real obstacle is not fixed placement but a continued unwillingness to advance.

claims.claim: Jiang recasts Piccarda's crisis as a problem of fear under coercion: when soldiers arrive, the decisive issue is whether she trusts God enough not to recoil from death or uncertainty.
Jiang says fear itself is the evidence of weak faith because genuine trust in God would remove terror of the soldiers and the unknown leap beyond them.
Jiang says Piccarda is stuck not because earthly actions permanently fix heavenly rank but because she still does not want to advance beyond her current state.
The student's follow-up makes explicit that heaven in this model remains mutable: growth is possible after death, but only if the will overcomes fear and wants more.
claims.temporal_scope: Student question and Jiang answer on 2026-06-15.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang reduces Piccarda's whole blockage to one interior fact: fear tells God you do not really want salvation enough.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is the packet's cleanest causal mechanism linking psychology, theology, and heavenly rank.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang says Piccarda is trapped by fear of the unknown leap of faith rather than by contentment or innocence alone.
signature_moments.source_phrase: she's afraid of that leap of faith
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This sharpens his reinterpretation from external victimhood to inner aversion at the threshold of transcendence.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The risk Jiang says Piccarda cannot take when fear keeps her from trusting God beyond immediate danger.
Jiang's explanation for why a person can remain spiritually stuck even without obvious external barriers.

chronology_notes.note: This June 15 packet pushes the will model into an account of fear, making heavenly stagnation reversible in principle but persistent wherever trust in God collapses into self-protective rationale.
